data.description:
## Symptom

An operator's local status change is silently reverted by the Jira reconciler, minutes later,
with every OTHER field write from the same period left intact. Confirmed twice on 2026-08-07:

- `858c-786a-13be-4332` (REB-2500): reopened `closed -> open` at 10:09:14Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> closed` at 10:17:58Z. The description rewrite from the same window SURVIVED.
- `556a-5a1f-adb3-4139` (REB-1504): moved `in_progress -> open` at 10:09:02Z; reconciler wrote
  `open -> in_progress` at 10:17:52Z.

Both events are authored `reconciler` / `env_id: reconciler`, e.g.
`.tickets-tracker/858c-786a-13be-4332/1786097878273766164-d80fab3f-...-STATUS.json`:
`{"author":"reconciler","env_id":"reconciler","data":{"current_status":"open","status":"closed"}}`.

The projection/reducer is NOT at fault: the reconciler event is genuinely the LATEST status
event in the log. This is an inbound write, not a replay defect.

## Proven root cause — the baseline lags our own outbound push by exactly one pass

ADR 0026 Decision 1 makes the per-binding baseline the sole direction signal:
`local == baseline` is taken to mean "local did not change, so a differing remote must be a
Jira-side edit — stand down and let inbound mirror it"
(`outbound_field_diff.py:323-334` `_suppressed_by_inbound`, applied to status at `:389-396`).
Inbound has no arbitration of its own — it is pure value inequality
(`inbound_differ.py:233-234`), and it only ever clobbers a field in a pass where outbound
emitted nothing for that field (same-pass suppression, `inbound_differ.py:709-718`).

The baseline is advanced from the pass-START snapshot (`reconcile.py:595` calling
`_advance_baselines`, `reconcile.py:514-531`, with `ctx.curr_snapshot` fetched at
`reconcile.py:280` BEFORE the outbound apply). So in the pass where rebar itself pushes a status
to Jira, the baseline is left holding the OLD value.

That makes the guard's premise false for one pass. A REOPEN is a revert to a previous value, so:

1. Pass N (run 31168795002): local `closed`/`in_progress` pushed outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description,status]` and
   `key=REB-1504 changed=[...,status]`. Jira now holds `Done` / `In Progress`.
   Baseline NOT advanced: `.bridge_state/bindings.json` at f0fe2ce9d4 (10:14:45Z) still records
   `baseline.status = 'To Do'` for BOTH bindings.
2. Operator reopens locally to `open` (10:09).
3. Pass N+1 (run 31169292024): local `open` == canonicalized baseline `To Do` -> `open`, so
   `_suppressed_by_inbound` fires and status is omitted from outbound —
   `RECON: outbound_update key=REB-2500 changed=[description]`, `key=REB-1504 changed=[]`.
   Inbound then reads Jira's `Done`/`In Progress` and overwrites local. Clobber.

This is the same omit-vs-clear asymmetry class recorded on `39c1-2a32-b564-4b4b` for the
2026-08-03 parent-clear incident (`ed5e-f176-3aea-41fd`).

### Runtime reproduction (the discriminating experiment)

Replaying the real pass-time inputs through `outbound_field_diff.compute_update_fields`, with the
baseline as the ONLY variable:

    STALE baseline 'To Do' (the real pass-time value)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW'}                     status_sent=False
    ADVANCED baseline 'Done' (what outbound had just pushed)
       -> outbound fields = {'description': 'NEW', 'status': 'To Do'}  status_sent=True

The stale-baseline row reproduces the observed `changed=[description]` exactly, including the
operator's discriminating detail: the description was NOT equal to the baseline so it WAS sent,
while status was suppressed. One variable flips the outcome.

## Why the description survived but the status did not

Not a revision rollback. Description differed from the (stale) baseline, so it was pushed
outbound and inbound had nothing to say. Status EQUALLED the stale baseline, so outbound stood
down and inbound won. The asymmetry is a direct consequence of the guard, not of event ordering.

## NOT a regression from 2026-08-07 changes

The clobbering pass is run 31169292024, started 10:14:54Z. Every suspect commit landed AFTER it:
e7a9 `33d6d4ef7c` 12:16:01Z, 851e `17c31cf5c8` 12:25:19Z, 2876 `c390cef54a` 12:34:40Z,
65d7 `08dfbbc689` 13:13:44Z. None was in the deployed tree.

Independently: a tracker-wide sweep for `author: reconciler` STATUS events finds the SAME shape
on 2026-07-20 15:21:03Z across 8 tickets (`0662-2b88-6fe3-4844`, `1416-b1bc-c8e9-477e`,
`542e-fb17-6f5d-4ced`, `caed-6c07-2a14-4ef9`, `7cab-bb99-9803-4ccb`, `9f60-2767-9ca3-45b2`,
`c03f-254f-014b-4cc7` open->closed, `6dac-d0d9-1a60-4998` in_progress->closed) — 18 days earlier.
Pre-existing defect, exposed today because the Reconcile Bridge was re-enabled mid-session.

## Blast radius

Any local status change made in the window between rebar's own outbound push of a status and the
next pass's baseline advance, where the new local value equals the pre-push baseline. Reopen and
un-claim are exactly that shape, so operator corrections are the most exposed operation. Silent:
the pass exits 0 and nothing is logged as a conflict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The baseline for a field is advanced to the value rebar itself just pushed outbound, so
      `local == baseline` no longer means "local unchanged" for one pass after our own write
      (or an equivalent fix that removes the false premise)
- [ ] A test reproduces the ABA sequence end to end - baseline B, local pushed to A, local
      reverted to B before the next pass - and proves the status is NOT clobbered
- [ ] A test pins that the deliberate ADR 0026 behaviour is NOT weakened: a genuine Jira-side
      status edit against an unchanged local status still flows inbound
- [ ] The fix is applied to every inbound-mirrored field, or its restriction to status is stated
      with a reason (`_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` = title, description, priority, status, assignee -
      all share the guard, so all share the ABA exposure)
data.title: Reconciler reverts a local status change: the arbitration baseline lags rebar's own outbound push by one pass, so a reopen looks like 'local never changed'
